name: org.thebgdb/mcp
title: The Board Game DB
description: Look up tens of thousands of board games: players, play time, designers, awards and rules.

tools.name: search_games
tools.description: Find board games whose name, in any language, contains every word of the query, best-known games first. Case, accents and punctuation are ignored, and typos are corrected (wingspn finds Wingspan; such games come last and are marked approximate). Returns each game's id, to use with get_game. Also returns, under people, up to 10 designers, artists, publishers and families whose name (or a spelling merged into it) starts at a word with the query (feld finds Stefan Feld), each with its credit kind and slug, to use with get_credit.

query.description: Part of the game's name, at least 2 characters.

tools.name: get_game
tools.description: Everything the catalog knows about one game: its names in every language, tagline, year, players, playing time, minimum age, official website, the cover image (the main one, the original edition's), the box of each other edition, name or language it is sold under (covers, each with its edition, name and language), and members' photos, each with what it shows (imageKind, and kind under images: box_front, box_back, components, cards, people…), the description (description: what the game is, its premise, its core, a turn, its components, how it ends, variants and editions, in plain text of up to 2,500 characters with paragraphs and dash lists; descriptionBlocks: the same as paragraphs and lists) (texts and images taken from other sources under a licence, such as Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, are credited on the site's /credits page), designers, artists, publishers (the original edition's publisher first, also as originalPublisher), categories, mechanics and families (under credits), awards with their year, category and result, related games (expansions, what it redoes or is redone by, what it is based on and its spin-offs, what it is part of, under relations), and what members say: rating, complexity, ranks, recommended age and votes on each number of players. A null field means unknown.

id.description: The game's id, from a search or list. Its slug works too.

tools.name: get_game_rules
tools.description: A game's rules in plain words, for one edition and language, in up to six sections (summary, setup, turn, end, scoring, variants), with who wrote each: a member, or a draft read from an uploaded rulebook in our own words and checked by a moderator (with that rulebook's files). A section the rulebook does not cover is left out. `editions` lists every edition and the languages it has rules in. Text uses light formatting: paragraphs, `- ` and `1. ` lists, **bold**.

id.description: The game's id, from a search or list. Its slug works too.

edition.description: An edition's id from `editions`. Without it, the original edition.

language.description: A language code such as "en" or "fr". Without it, or when there is nothing in it: English, then any.

tools.name: get_game_tutorial
tools.description: How to play a game step by step, for one edition and language: each step's text, with one image (a path on the API) or one video link, and who wrote it. `editions` lists every edition and the languages it has a tutorial in.

id.description: The game's id, from a search or list. Its slug works too.

edition.description: An edition's id from `editions`. Without it, the original edition.

language.description: A language code such as "en" or "fr". Without it, or when there is nothing in it: English, then any.

tools.name: list_games
tools.description: Browse the catalog a page at a time, narrowed by number of players, year, playing time, age, complexity or rating, in the order asked. Pass the returned nextCursor to get the next page.

players.description: Only games that play with this many.

players_from.description: With players_to: only games that play at every count in the range.

time_max.description: A game fits in this many minutes.

age.description: Suitable for a player of this age.

complexity_max.description: Complexity as voted by members, 1 (light) to 5 (heavy).

rating_min.description: Average member rating of at least this, out of 10.

illustrated.description: Only games that have a cover image.

order.description: name: A to Z. year: most recent game first. oldest: oldest game first. new: latest additions first. hot: most looked at and rated lately. rating: best rated by members. complexity: heaviest first.

tools.name: list_credits
tools.description: List one kind of credit with the number of games linked to each. A family is a series or a group of games that belong together. Use prefix to find a name (for example kind=designers, prefix=Knizia will not match: prefixes match the start of the full name, so use prefix=Reiner).

prefix.description: Only names starting with this text.

tools.name: get_credit
tools.description: The games linked to one credit, 60 at a time, most recently added first unless an order is given; pass the returned nextCursor for the next page. The same filters as list_games apply. An award also comes with its years and the games honoured each year. Example: kind=designers, slug=reiner-knizia, players=2, order=rating.

tools.name: anniversaries
tools.description: Games whose age this year is a multiple of five (the catalog knows publication years, not days).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search board games by name. Returns results with an id to pass to fetch.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full record of a game, by the id returned by search, as JSON text: its names in every language, tagline, year, players, playing time, minimum age, official website, the cover image (the main one, the original edition's), the box of each other edition, name or language it is sold under (covers, each with its edition, name and language), and members' photos, each with what it shows (imageKind, and kind under images: box_front, box_back, components, cards, people…), the description (description: what the game is, its premise, its core, a turn, its components, how it ends, variants and editions, in plain text of up to 2,500 characters with paragraphs and dash lists; descriptionBlocks: the same as paragraphs and lists) (texts and images taken from other sources under a licence, such as Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, are credited on the site's /credits page), designers, artists, publishers (the original edition's publisher first, also as originalPublisher), categories, mechanics and families (under credits), awards with their year, category and result, related games (expansions, what it redoes or is redone by, what it is based on and its spin-offs, what it is part of, under relations), and what members say: rating, complexity, ranks, recommended age and votes on each number of players.
